name: Nobody Asked for This!

pick.label: Pick a sponsor
pick.heading: Pick a brand and make it sponsor a tour
lead: Brands pay a fortune to put their name next to music: on festivals, arenas, tours and sometimes the artist's T-shirt. Some partnerships feel completely natural. Others feel like a very expensive mistake.
Choose a brand and invent the tour it sponsors. The less obvious the match, the better. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *Make us believe it.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: I'm not looking for a real contract here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some deals will make total sense and some will only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: Which brand is paying? From the shelf or your own idea.
A real artist or band. The more unexpected the match, the better.
What does it say on the posters? Is the brand's name in it?
Its logo on the stage, its product in the show, adverts, something stranger?
Why would fans be happy about this instead of rolling their eyes?
What happens if the artist, the brand or the fans hate it?

values.artist: Helene Fischer. 'Atemlos durch die Nacht' is exactly how it feels to run for a connecting ICE.
values.tour: DB presents: Atemlos durch die Nacht – The Slightly Delayed Tour.
values.gets: Its logo on the stage, and every show starts with the famous announcement: 'Due to a delay in the operational process, this concert will begin approximately twenty minutes late.'
values.fans: A free BahnCard 25 with every ticket, and a guaranteed seat (at the concert, not on the train).
values.wrong: Helene arrives forty minutes late because of a signal failure near Fulda. To be fair, that's very on-brand.
